questions.q: Why isn't SELECT privilege on a table alone enough for a role to actually query it, per this lesson?
options: The role also needs USAGE privilege on the schema, just to reference objects inside it at all
PostgreSQL requires SUPERUSER for any SELECT statement
SELECT privilege is granted automatically to every role by default
Table-level privileges do not exist in PostgreSQL
questions.explain: Schema USAGE is a separate, required layer — without it a role can't 'see into' the schema even with table-level SELECT granted.

questions.q: How does ownership work in PostgreSQL, per this lesson?
options: The role that creates an object owns it and automatically has full privileges on it, regardless of any GRANT statement
Ownership is purely metadata with no effect on privileges
Only a SUPERUSER role can ever own any object
Ownership is assigned randomly to any role with CONNECT privilege
questions.explain: Ownership itself is a privilege source in PostgreSQL, closer to Unix file ownership than SQL Server's grant-centric model.

questions.q: What real problem does ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES solve, per this lesson?
options: It automatically grants specified privileges on objects created in the future by a given role in a given schema
It retroactively grants access to every object that already exists in a database
It revokes all privileges from a role immediately
It changes the default authentication method in pg_hba.conf
questions.explain: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES applies only to future objects created after the statement runs — not existing ones — solving the problem of keeping access current as new objects appear.

questions.q: Is ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES retroactive, per this lesson?
options: No — it only affects objects created after the statement runs
Yes — it immediately applies to every existing object in the schema
Yes, but only for tables, not sequences or other object types
It is retroactive only if the role has SUPERUSER
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly notes ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES is not retroactive; it only governs objects created after it is set up.

questions.q: How do you transfer ownership of a table to a different role, per this lesson?
options: ALTER TABLE ... OWNER TO new_role;
GRANT OWNERSHIP ON TABLE ... TO new_role;
REVOKE ALL ON TABLE ... FROM old_role;
Ownership in PostgreSQL cannot be transferred once set
questions.explain: ALTER TABLE ... OWNER TO new_role; is the real PostgreSQL syntax for transferring ownership of a table to another role.
